problem.passage: During the 1930s, city planners in Curitiba, Brazil, began experimenting with dedicated bus corridors long before the term "bus rapid transit" existed. Decades later, in the 1970s, the mayor's administration formalized this approach, and ______
problem.stimulus: During the 1930s, city planners in Curitiba, Brazil, began experimenting with dedicated bus corridors long before the term "bus rapid transit" existed. Decades later, in the 1970s, the mayor's administration formalized this approach, and ______
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: transportation officials around the world eventually studied the system that resulted, it became known as one of the most efficient networks on the continent
transportation officials around the world eventually studied the system that resulted, which became known as one of the most efficient networks on the continent
transportation officials around the world eventually studied the system that resulted; it became one of the most, efficient networks on the continent
transportation officials around the world eventually studied the system that resulted; becoming known as one of the most efficient networks on the continent
problem.explanation: 두 번째 선택지는 관계대명사 'which'를 사용해 앞 절을 수식하는 종속절을 만들어 두 개의 독립절이 쉼표만으로 잘못 연결되는 콤마 스플라이스를 피한다. 첫 번째 선택지는 'the system that resulted'와 'it became known...'이 각각 독립절인데 쉼표 하나로만 이어져 있어 콤마 스플라이스 오류다. 세 번째 선택지는 세미콜론 뒤에 독립절이 오지만, 'one of the most, efficient'처럼 형용사구 사이에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 수식 관계를 훼손한다. 네 번째 선택지는 세미콜론 뒤에 'becoming known...'이라는 분사구(불완전한 절)를 붙여 세미콜론이 요구하는 독립절 조건을 어긴다.
problem.evidenceSpan: transportation officials around the world eventually studied the system that resulted, it became known as one of the most efficient networks on the continent
problem.answerRationale: 정답은 'which'로 시작하는 종속절을 사용해 두 개의 완전한 절을 쉼표만으로 이어 붙이는 콤마 스플라이스를 피하면서 앞 절에 대한 부가 설명을 자연스럽게 연결한다.

difficultyReasons: 두 독립절을 올바르게 연결하는 방법(콤마+관계대명사 which vs 세미콜론 vs 콤마 스플라이스)을 구분해야 함 - 2단계 추론
선택지들이 콤마 오류, 세미콜론 뒤 불완전한 절, 불필요한 콤마 삽입 등 서로 다른 문법 오류를 포함하고 있어 각각을 정확히 판별해야 함
B와 A는 표면적으로 거의 동일하여 which/it 차이를 정확히 인지해야 정답을 고를 수 있음

distractors.plausibleBecause: 두 독립절을 연결하려는 시도로 보이며, 콤마로 연결된 것처럼 보일 수 있어 문법을 자세히 보지 않으면 자연스러워 보인다
distractors.matches: studied the system that resulted, 뒤에 이어지는 절의 내용(효율적 네트워크로 알려짐)과 의미상 일치
distractors.whyWrong: 콤마만으로 두 개의 독립절(studied...resulted / it became known...)을 연결하는 것은 comma splice(콤마 접속 오류)로 표준 영어 문법에 어긋난다

distractors.plausibleBecause: 세미콜론으로 두 독립절을 올바르게 연결한 것처럼 보이고, most 다음 콤마가 사소해 보여 지나치기 쉽다
distractors.matches: 세미콜론 사용은 B의 구조와 유사하게 두 절을 분리한다는 점에서 일치
distractors.whyWrong: 'most, efficient'처럼 최상급 표현 중간에 불필요한 콤마가 삽입되어 문법적으로 틀리다

distractors.plausibleBecause: 세미콜론 뒤에 분사구를 붙여 부가 설명을 하는 것처럼 보여 자연스럽게 읽힐 수 있다
distractors.matches: studied...resulted 뒤에 becoming known...이라는 내용이 이어진다는 점에서 의미상 연결된다
distractors.whyWrong: 세미콜론 뒤에는 독립절이 와야 하는데 'becoming known...'은 분사구로 완전한 문장이 아니어서 문법적으로 틀린 구조(sentence fragment)이다

problem.passage:
Byzantine mosaic artists working in the sixth century faced a practical problem: how to make flat walls and ceilings appear to shimmer with divine light. Their solution was to set thousands of small glass tesserae, backed with gold leaf, at slightly irregular angles rather than in a perfectly smooth plane. Because the tiny gold surfaces tilted in many directions, they caught candlelight and sunlight differently depending on where a viewer stood, producing a flickering, luminous effect that a flat, evenly set surface could never achieve. This deliberate irregularity, rather than being a flaw in craftsmanship, was a calculated technique for transforming static images into scenes that seemed to glow with an inner light.

According to the text, why did Byzantine mosaic artists set gold tesserae at irregular angles?
problem.stimulus: Byzantine mosaic artists working in the sixth century faced a practical problem: how to make flat walls and ceilings appear to shimmer with divine light. Their solution was to set thousands of small glass tesserae, backed with gold leaf, at slightly irregular angles rather than in a perfectly smooth plane. Because the tiny gold surfaces tilted in many directions, they caught candlelight and sunlight differently depending on where a viewer stood, producing a flickering, luminous effect that a flat, evenly set surface could never achieve. This deliberate irregularity, rather than being a flaw in craftsmanship, was a calculated technique for transforming static images into scenes that seemed to glow with an inner light.
problem.question: According to the text, why did Byzantine mosaic artists set gold tesserae at irregular angles?
options: They wanted the gold leaf to remain visible to viewers no matter which direction the tesserae faced.
They lacked the tools needed to set the tesserae in a perfectly smooth, flat plane.
They aimed to create a shimmering, luminous effect by having the tiles reflect light differently from different angles.
They wanted to prevent the glass tesserae from loosening or falling off the wall over time.
problem.explanation: 지문은 예술가들이 테세라를 불규칙한 각도로 배치한 이유를 명확히 설명한다. 작은 금박 표면들이 여러 방향으로 기울어져 있어 빛을 다르게 반사시켰고, 이로 인해 반짝이는 광채 효과가 만들어졌다는 것이다. 또한 지문은 마지막 문장에서 이것이 기술 부족이 아니라 '계산된 기법'이었다고 명시한다. C는 이 인과관계를 정확히 담고 있다. A는 지문에 언급되지 않은 내용을 지어낸 것이다. B는 '기술 부족' 때문이라는 지문이 명시적으로 부정한 설명을 오답으로 제시한다. D는 지문이 말하는 각도 배치의 목적(빛 반사 효과)이 아니라 색상 패턴이라는 지문에 없는 세부에 초점을 맞춘 오답이다.
problem.evidenceTarget: 지문 전체가 설명하는 중심 인과관계: 비잔틴 모자이크 예술가들이 금박 테세라를 불규칙한 각도로 배치한 목적
problem.evidenceSpan: Because the tiny gold surfaces tilted in many directions, they caught candlelight and sunlight differently depending on where a viewer stood, producing a flickering, luminous effect that a flat, evenly set surface could never achieve.
problem.answerRationale: evidence_span은 불규칙한 각도 배치(원인)와 빛을 다르게 반사하여 생기는 반짝이는 광채 효과(결과)를 직접 연결하므로, 이 인과관계를 그대로 표현한 선택지가 정답이다.

difficultyReasons: 정답 도출에 필요한 추론이 1단계로 지문의 핵심 문장을 그대로 재진술하면 됨
오답들이 지문의 표현과 명백히 반대되거나 무관하여 변별이 쉬움
비교나 조건, 시간관계 등 미묘한 요소가 없음
지문 자체가 짧고 핵심 문장이 명확하게 제시됨

distractors.plausibleBecause: 지문에 '금 표면이 여러 방향으로 기울어져 있다'는 내용이 있어 gold leaf가 항상 보이도록 했다는 식으로 오해할 수 있음
distractors.matches: gold surfaces tilted in many directions라는 문구와 표면적으로 연결됨
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 금박이 항상 보이게 하려는 목적이 아니라, 각도가 달라 빛을 다르게 반사해 반짝이는 효과를 내려는 목적이라고 명시함

distractors.plausibleBecause: 불규칙한 배치를 기술 부족이나 도구 부족으로 오해할 수 있음
distractors.matches: irregular angles라는 표현과 피상적으로 연결됨
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 이러한 불규칙성이 '기교의 결함이 아니라 의도적인 기법(calculated technique)'이라고 명시적으로 부정함

distractors.plausibleBecause: 타일이 떨어지지 않게 하려는 실용적 목적으로 오해할 수 있음
distractors.matches: 지문에 없는 내용이지만 모자이크 제작의 일반적 상식과 연결될 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: 지문에는 타일의 내구성이나 고정에 관한 언급이 전혀 없음

issues: 해설 마지막 문장에서 D 선택지를 설명할 때 '색상 패턴'이라는 표현을 사용했는데, 실제 D 선택지는 색상 패턴이 아니라 '타일이 벽에서 헐거워지거나 떨어지는 것을 방지'하는 내용에 관한 것이므로 해설과 선택지 내용이 일치하지 않음. 해설의 D에 대한 설명이 부정확함.

problem.passage:
Economists studying the collapse of the Dutch tulip market in 1637 have often described it as history's first speculative bubble, driven purely by irrational public enthusiasm for rare flower bulbs. Yet a closer look at contract records from the period complicates this narrative. Most of the trading that drove prices to their peak occurred not through cash purchases but through futures contracts, agreements to buy bulbs at a fixed price on a future date, often made among a relatively small circle of merchants rather than the general public. When a regional outbreak of plague disrupted trade routes and reduced the number of buyers able to honor these contracts, prices collapsed rapidly, suggesting that the crash was tied as much to a breakdown in a narrow contract market as to widespread public mania.

According to the text, what does a closer look at contract records suggest about the 1637 tulip market collapse?
problem.stimulus: Economists studying the collapse of the Dutch tulip market in 1637 have often described it as history's first speculative bubble, driven purely by irrational public enthusiasm for rare flower bulbs. Yet a closer look at contract records from the period complicates this narrative. Most of the trading that drove prices to their peak occurred not through cash purchases but through futures contracts, agreements to buy bulbs at a fixed price on a future date, often made among a relatively small circle of merchants rather than the general public. When a regional outbreak of plague disrupted trade routes and reduced the number of buyers able to honor these contracts, prices collapsed rapidly, suggesting that the crash was tied as much to a breakdown in a narrow contract market as to widespread public mania.
problem.question: According to the text, what does a closer look at contract records suggest about the 1637 tulip market collapse?
options: The collapse was caused entirely by ordinary members of the public buying and selling bulbs for cash.
The collapse resulted only from a plague outbreak that had nothing to do with the structure of trading contracts.
The collapse was tied to the breakdown of a narrow futures contract market among merchants, not just widespread public mania.
The collapse proves that speculative bubbles never involve any element of public enthusiasm or irrational behavior.
problem.explanation: 지문은 처음에 튤립 시장 붕괴가 순전히 대중의 비합리적 열광 때문이라는 통념을 소개한 뒤, 계약 기록을 근거로 이를 복잡하게 만든다. 실제 거래 대부분은 현금 매매가 아니라 소수 상인 사이의 선물 계약을 통해 이뤄졌고, 전염병으로 인해 계약을 이행할 구매자가 줄어들자 가격이 급락했다는 것이다. 지문은 이를 '대중적 광기만큼이나 좁은 계약 시장의 붕괴'와도 관련이 있다고 결론짓는다. C는 이 인과관계를 정확히 반영한다. A는 지문이 실제로 부정하는, 현금 거래를 통한 대중적 매매라는 통념을 그대로 제시한다. B는 전염병만이 유일한 원인이며 계약 구조와 무관하다고 주장해 지문이 강조하는 계약 시장과의 연관성을 완전히 빠뜨린다. D는 지문에 없는 극단적 일반화(투기적 거품은 대중의 열광과 전혀 무관하다)로, 지문은 오히려 대중적 광기도 어느 정도 요인이었을 수 있음을 인정한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text first introduces the common view that the tulip market collapse was driven purely by irrational public enthusiasm, then complicates this using contract records: most trading occurred through futures contracts among a small circle of merchants rather than cash purchases by the public, and prices collapsed when a plague outbreak reduced the number of buyers able to honor these contracts. The text concludes that the crash was tied 'as much to a breakdown in a narrow contract market as to widespread public mania.' Choice C accurately reflects this causal relationship. Choice A restates the very popular narrative the evidence complicates. Choice B claims the plague was the sole cause with no connection to contract structure, omitting the contract-market link the text emphasizes. Choice D makes an unsupported overgeneralization, since the text does not deny that public mania played any role at all.

distractorRationales.plausible_because: 지문 처음에 소개된 통념과 일치해 그럴듯하다
distractorRationales.why_wrong: 지문은 계약 기록을 통해 이 통념을 복잡하게 만들며, 실제로는 현금 매매가 아니라 선물 계약이 주된 거래 방식이었다고 명시한다

distractorRationales.plausible_because: 전염병이 실제 원인의 일부로 언급되어 그럴듯하다
distractorRationales.why_wrong: 지문은 전염병이 계약 시장 구조와 결합해 작용했다고 설명하며, 계약 구조와 무관하다는 주장은 핵심 관계를 놓친 것이다

distractorRationales.matches: 지문이 통념을 복잡하게 만든다는 전체 논조
distractorRationales.plausible_because: 대중적 열광 서사를 반박하는 듯한 논조와 표면적으로 이어진다
distractorRationales.why_wrong: 지문은 대중적 광기의 역할을 완전히 부정하지 않고 그것과 '함께' 계약 시장 붕괴도 작용했다고 말하므로, 이는 지나친 일반화다

problem.evidenceTarget: 지문에서 명시한 세부 정보 — 계약 기록이 시사하는 1637년 튤립 시장 붕괴의 실제 성격
problem.evidenceSpan: suggesting that the crash was tied as much to a breakdown in a narrow contract market as to widespread public mania
problem.answerRationale: 지문은 거래 대부분이 선물 계약을 통해 소수 상인 사이에서 이뤄졌고, 전염병으로 계약 이행이 어려워지며 가격이 붕괴했다고 설명해 대중적 광기뿐 아니라 좁은 계약 시장의 붕괴도 원인이었음을 보여준다.

difficultyReasons: 정답 문장이 지문 마지막 문장과 거의 동일한 표현으로 제시되어 대조 단계가 1단계에 불과함
오답들이 all/never/only/entirely 같은 과장된 절대 표현을 포함해 쉽게 배제 가능함

distractors.plausibleBecause: 지문이 '순수한 대중의 열광'이라는 통념을 언급하고 있어, 대중이 관련되었다는 인상을 받을 수 있다
distractors.matches: 지문 첫 문장의 'irrational public enthusiasm'이라는 표현과 표면적으로 연결됨
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 오히려 거래가 현금 구매가 아닌 선물 계약을 통해, 소수 상인 집단 사이에서 이루어졌다고 명시하므로 '전적으로 일반 대중의 현금 거래'라는 진술은 지문 내용과 정반대

distractors.plausibleBecause: 흑사병이 계약 이행 실패의 직접적 원인으로 언급되어 이것이 유일한 원인처럼 보일 수 있다
distractors.matches: 'a regional outbreak of plague disrupted trade routes and reduced the number of buyers able to honor these contracts'라는 문장과 일치
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 흑사병이 계약 구조(선물 계약, 좁은 상인 집단)와 결합되어 붕괴를 초래했다고 설명하며, 계약 구조와 무관하다는 진술은 인과관계를 왜곡함

distractors.plausibleBecause: 지문이 기존 통념(순수 대중 열광)을 반박하는 듯한 어조를 취해, 대중의 열광이 전혀 없었다는 극단적 결론으로 오인할 수 있다
distractors.matches: 지문이 'complicates this narrative'라며 기존 설명에 의문을 제기하는 부분과 표면적으로 연결됨
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 이 사건이 대중 열광과 무관하다고 하지 않고, 계약 시장 붕괴가 '대중 열광만큼이나' 중요했다고 언급하며, 투기 거품 일반에 대한 절대적 진술은 전혀 하지 않음

problem.passage:
When cities widen highways to reduce traffic congestion, engineers often find that congestion returns within a few years, sometimes worse than before. This outcome is not a failure of construction but a predictable consequence of what transportation planners call induced demand: when a road's capacity increases, driving becomes more convenient relative to other options, so more people choose to drive, take longer trips, or shift their commute onto the newly widened route. The additional capacity is absorbed by this new traffic, and congestion levels drift back toward where they started. As a result, many transportation researchers now argue that widening roads is rarely a durable solution to congestion on its own.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: When cities widen highways to reduce traffic congestion, engineers often find that congestion returns within a few years, sometimes worse than before. This outcome is not a failure of construction but a predictable consequence of what transportation planners call induced demand: when a road's capacity increases, driving becomes more convenient relative to other options, so more people choose to drive, take longer trips, or shift their commute onto the newly widened route. The additional capacity is absorbed by this new traffic, and congestion levels drift back toward where they started. As a result, many transportation researchers now argue that widening roads is rarely a durable solution to congestion on its own.

options: Congestion returns because construction crews often fail to build enough additional lanes to handle existing traffic.

Transportation planners have coined the term induced demand to describe how commuters choose longer routes.
Cities should stop widening highways altogether and invest exclusively in public transportation instead.
problem.explanation: 지문은 도로를 넓혀도 몇 년 안에 정체가 되돌아오는 현상을 설명하며, 그 원인이 시공 부실이 아니라 '유발수요'라는 개념 때문이라고 밝힌다. 도로 용량이 늘면 운전이 더 편리해져 더 많은 사람이 운전을 선택하게 되고, 그 결과 새로 생긴 용량이 다시 소진된다는 것이다. 마지막 문장은 이를 근거로 확장이 지속적인 해결책이 아니라고 결론짓는다. B는 이 전체 논리를 정확히 담고 있다. A는 정체가 돌아오는 이유를 시공 부실로 잘못 짚어 인과관계를 왜곡한다. C는 유발수요라는 용어의 정의 일부만 다루며 범위를 지나치게 좁혔다. D는 지문에 없는 '대중교통에만 투자해야 한다'는 정책 제안을 지어내 지문이 실제로 주장하지 않은 내용이다.
problem.explanationEn: The text explains that congestion returns within a few years of highway widening, and attributes this not to poor construction but to the concept of induced demand: greater road capacity makes driving more attractive, so more people drive, absorbing the new capacity. The final sentence concludes that widening is rarely a durable fix. Choice B captures this full line of reasoning. Choice A misidentifies the cause as construction failure, reversing the actual causal explanation. Choice C only restates part of the definition of induced demand, which is too narrow to be the main idea. Choice D proposes a specific policy (investing exclusively in public transit) that the text never states, making it unsupported by the passage.

problem.passage:
Botanists studying the corpse flower (Amorphophallus titanum) have long been fascinated by its rare and dramatic bloom, which can take seven to ten years to occur and lasts only about forty-eight hours. During this brief window, the plant releases a odor resembling rotting flesh, a trait that once seemed like a strange evolutionary accident. Recent field research in Sumatra, however, has shown that the smell is a precise adaptation for attracting carrion beetles and flesh flies, insects that normally lay their eggs in decaying animal matter. By mimicking the scent and even the reddish color of rotting meat, the corpse flower tricks these insects into entering its bloom, where they inadvertently collect and transfer pollen before flying off to another flowering plant. Far from being an accident, the flower's foul smell is a highly specific reproductive strategy honed by natural selection to exploit the sensory habits of a particular set of pollinators.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Botanists studying the corpse flower (Amorphophallus titanum) have long been fascinated by its rare and dramatic bloom, which can take seven to ten years to occur and lasts only about forty-eight hours. options: The corpse flower's rare, multi-year blooming cycle is the main reason botanists consider it an evolutionary accident rather than a deliberate adaptation.

problem.explanation: 지문은 시체꽃의 악취가 오랫동안 '이상한 진화적 우연'처럼 보였지만, 최근 연구에서 이는 특정 곤충(시체 딱정벌레와 파리)을 유인해 수분을 돕도록 자연선택이 정교하게 다듬은 번식 전략임이 밝혀졌다고 설명한다. 마지막 문장에서 '우연이 아니라 특정 수분매개자의 감각 습성을 이용하도록 진화한 매우 구체적인 번식 전략'이라고 명확히 정리하므로, 이것이 지문 전체의 중심 생각이다. B는 이를 정확히 요약한다. A는 개화 주기라는 부수적 세부사항에 그치고, C는 곤충이 '우연히' 방문한다고 말해 지문의 정교한 유인 전략이라는 핵심을 왜곡하며, D는 색이 포식자를 쫓기 위한 것이라는, 지문에 없는 내용을 지어낸 것이다.
problem.explanationEn: The text explains that the corpse flower's foul smell, once considered a strange evolutionary accident, has recently been shown to be a precise adaptation: it lures specific insects (carrion beetles and flesh flies) to aid pollination. The final sentence explicitly states that the smell is 'a highly specific reproductive strategy honed by natural selection to exploit the sensory habits of a particular set of pollinators,' making this the text's central idea. Choice B accurately captures this. Choice A focuses only on the blooming cycle, a minor supporting detail. Choice C distorts the causal relationship by suggesting insects visit 'occasionally' or by chance, when the text describes a deliberate deceptive strategy. Choice D invents an unsupported claim that the flower's color serves to frighten predators, which the text never states.

problem.passage:
The deep-sea anglerfish is famous for the bioluminescent lure that dangles from its head, but this light-producing organ is only one part of a broader survival strategy. In the pitch-black waters below 1,000 meters, food is scarce and encounters between individuals are rare, so anglerfish have evolved traits that maximize every opportunity: an enormous, hinged jaw capable of swallowing prey larger than itself, a stomach that expands to store rare meals, and, in many species, a lure whose glow is produced by symbiotic bacteria. Together these adaptations allow the fish to survive for long stretches without eating and to make the most of the infrequent meals it does encounter.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.explanation: 지문은 첫 문장에서 발광 기관이 '더 넓은 생존 전략의 한 부분일 뿐'이라고 명시하고, 이어서 턱, 위, 발광 기관을 함께 열거하며 이 모두가 협력해 먹이가 드문 환경에서 생존을 돕는다고 설명한다. 정답 선택지는 이 전체 요지—여러 형질이 함께 작용한다는 점—를 정확히 담고 있다. 첫 번째 오답(발광 기관의 원리만 언급)은 지문에 언급된 세부 사항이지만 하나의 적응 형질에만 초점을 맞춰 범위가 좁다(TOO_NARROW_DETAIL). 두 번째 오답(심해 환경 자체의 특징)은 배경 설명일 뿐 아귀의 적응 자체를 다루지 않아 초점이 빗나간다(WRONG_FOCUS). 세 번째 오답은 위(stomach)라는 하나의 적응 형질에 대한 세부 내용을 마치 지문 전체의 핵심 결론인 것처럼 과장되게 일반화하여 다른 두 형질(턱, 발광 기관)을 배제한 진술이므로 지나치게 일반화된 오류이다(OVERGENERALIZED).

problem.passage:
During the 1870s, a wave of small, independently owned general stores across rural America began to struggle as regional wholesalers introduced new distribution networks that connected farmers directly to manufacturers. Historians studying this period initially attributed the stores' decline primarily to competition from early mail-order catalogs, which could offer lower prices on manufactured goods. However, account books and correspondence from the era reveal that many of these general stores closed years before mail-order catalogs became widely available in their regions. The more consistent factor appears to have been the wholesalers' new rail-based distribution routes, which let farmers bypass local storekeepers and order supplies directly, months or even years before catalog shopping became common.

According to the text, what does evidence from account books and correspondence suggest about the decline of rural general stores?
problem.stimulus: During the 1870s, a wave of small, independently owned general stores across rural America began to struggle as regional wholesalers introduced new distribution networks that connected farmers directly to manufacturers. Historians studying this period initially attributed the stores' decline primarily to competition from early mail-order catalogs, which could offer lower prices on manufactured goods. However, account books and correspondence from the era reveal that many of these general stores closed years before mail-order catalogs became widely available in their regions. The more consistent factor appears to have been the wholesalers' new rail-based distribution routes, which let farmers bypass local storekeepers and order supplies directly, months or even years before catalog shopping became common.
problem.question: According to the text, what does evidence from account books and correspondence suggest about the decline of rural general stores?
options: The stores declined mainly because farmers preferred the lower prices offered in mail-order catalogs.
The stores' decline began before mail-order catalogs were common, pointing instead to new rail-based distribution routes as the more consistent cause.
The stores declined because wholesalers and mail-order catalogs together completely replaced every function that local storekeepers once served.
The stores declined because farmers increasingly distrusted local storekeepers and sought more reliable suppliers elsewhere.
problem.explanation: 지문은 역사가들이 처음에는 우편주문 카탈로그를 쇠퇴의 주된 원인으로 지목했다고 밝히지만, 실제 회계 장부와 서신 자료는 다른 이야기를 전한다고 설명한다. 많은 잡화점이 카탈로그가 널리 보급되기 '몇 년 전'에 이미 문을 닫았고, 더 일관된 원인은 도매상의 새로운 철도 기반 유통 경로였다는 것이다. 정답 선택지는 이 시간 관계와 인과관계를 정확히 반영한다. A는 지문이 처음에 제시했다가 자료로 반박하는 가설을 정답인 것처럼 제시해 시간 관계를 뒤바꾼 것이다(WRONG_FOCUS: 반박된 원래 가설에 초점을 맞춤). C는 지문에 언급된 두 요인(도매상 유통망, 카탈로그)을 가져오되 '모든 기능을 완전히 대체했다'는 식으로 지문이 뒷받침하지 않는 정도까지 과장한 것이다(OVERGENERALIZED: 지문의 제한된 설명을 전면적 대체로 부풀림). D는 지문에 전혀 등장하지 않는 '신뢰 상실'이라는 근거 없는 동기를 지어낸 것이다(UNSUPPORTED_BY_TEXT: 지문에 없는 내용을 창작함).
problem.evidenceTarget: 지문이 회계 장부·서신 증거를 근거로 실제로 밝히는 잡화점 쇠퇴의 핵심 원인(시간 순서상 카탈로그 이전, 철도 기반 유통망이 더 일관된 원인)
problem.evidenceSpan: account books and correspondence from the era reveal that many of these general stores closed years before mail-order catalogs became widely available in their regions. The more consistent factor appears to have been the wholesalers' new rail-based distribution routes
problem.answerRationale: 지문은 카탈로그 확산 '이전'에 폐업이 이미 일어났다는 시간적 사실과, 철도 기반 유통망이 더 '일관된' 원인이라는 인과 판단을 함께 제시하므로, 두 요소(시간 선후 관계 + 더 일관된 원인 지목)를 모두 담은 선택지만 정답이 될 수 있다.

오답 A는 지문 초반의 초기 가설을 반영하지만 지문이 이를 명시적으로 반박하므로 주의 깊게 읽으면 쉽게 걸러진다

problem.passage: Coral reefs are often described as the "rainforests of the sea" because of their extraordinary biodiversity, but this comparison obscures a critical vulnerability that distinguishes reefs from terrestrial rainforests. Rainforest ecosystems, while sensitive to deforestation, rest on soil and root systems that can persist and regenerate even after significant canopy loss. Coral reefs, by contrast, are built by the calcium carbonate skeletons of the coral organisms themselves; when rising ocean temperatures trigger coral bleaching, the polyps do not merely lose their color and productivity, they often die outright, and with them the physical structure that sustains the reef community disintegrates. Once that structural foundation crumbles, the thousands of fish, mollusk, and crustacean species that depend on reef architecture for shelter and breeding grounds lose their habitat entirely, not merely a food source or temporary shelter. This is why marine biologists increasingly argue that reef degradation, unlike deforestation, can cross a threshold beyond which recovery within a human lifetime becomes essentially impossible, since the very scaffolding of the ecosystem, not just its inhabitants, must be rebuilt from scratch by generations of slow-growing coral.
problem.stimulus: Coral reefs are often described as the "rainforests of the sea" because of their extraordinary biodiversity, but this comparison obscures a critical vulnerability that distinguishes reefs from terrestrial rainforests. Rainforest ecosystems, while sensitive to deforestation, rest on soil and root systems that can persist and regenerate even after significant canopy loss. Coral reefs, by contrast, are built by the calcium carbonate skeletons of the coral organisms themselves; when rising ocean temperatures trigger coral bleaching, the polyps do not merely lose their color and productivity, they often die outright, and with them the physical structure that sustains the reef community disintegrates. Once that structural foundation crumbles, the thousands of fish, mollusk, and crustacean species that depend on reef architecture for shelter and breeding grounds lose their habitat entirely, not merely a food source or temporary shelter. This is why marine biologists increasingly argue that reef degradation, unlike deforestation, can cross a threshold beyond which recovery within a human lifetime becomes essentially impossible, since the very scaffolding of the ecosystem, not just its inhabitants, must be rebuilt from scratch by generations of slow-growing coral.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Coral reefs support a greater number of species than rainforests do, which makes their loss more damaging to global biodiversity than deforestation.
Because coral bleaching destroys the structural foundation that reef organisms depend on, reef loss can be far harder to reverse than rainforest deforestation.
Rising ocean temperatures cause coral polyps to lose their color and productivity, a process known as coral bleaching that threatens marine food webs.
Marine biologists have concluded that coral reefs and rainforests should no longer be compared because the two ecosystems have entirely unrelated causes of decline.
problem.explanation: 지문은 산호초가 '바다의 열대우림'으로 불리지만 이 비유가 중요한 차이를 가린다고 지적하며, 해수 온도 상승이 백화를 일으키고 이는 단순한 색 손실이 아니라 폴립의 사멸로 이어져 산호초의 물리적 구조 자체가 무너진다는 점, 그리고 그 결과 열대우림과 달리 산호초는 인간 생애 내에 회복되기 어렵다는 점을 논증한다. 따라서 정답은 이러한 인과관계와 비교를 모두 담은 B번이다. A번은 생물다양성 규모 비교에 그쳐 회복 불가능성이라는 핵심을 놓치고, C번은 백화 과정 자체만 설명할 뿐 지문의 결론(회복 불가능성)을 담지 못하며, D번은 지문에 없는 '더 이상 비교하지 말아야 한다'는 주장을 지어낸 것이다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage argues that although coral reefs are called the "rainforests of the sea," this comparison masks a crucial difference: rising ocean temperatures cause bleaching that is not merely a loss of color but the actual death of coral polyps, which destroys the reef's physical structure—unlike rainforest soil and roots, which can persist. As a result, reef loss is far harder to reverse than deforestation. Choice B captures both this causal chain and the comparison, making it correct. Choice A focuses only on biodiversity scale, missing the recovery-difficulty argument. Choice C describes only the bleaching process, a supporting detail rather than the main idea. Choice D invents a claim—that biologists say the two ecosystems should no longer be compared—that the text never makes.

problem.passage: When city planners in the mid-twentieth century began replacing streetcar lines with bus routes across many American cities, the change was often justified as a straightforward upgrade: buses required no fixed rails, could be rerouted instantly, and cost far less to maintain than track and overhead wire systems. Yet transportation historians examining ridership records from this period have found that the shift produced a paradox. Even though buses were cheaper to operate per mile, ridership on former streetcar corridors frequently declined by twenty to thirty percent within a few years of conversion, eroding the very fare revenue that was supposed to offset the maintenance savings. Historians attribute this decline not to any inherent flaw in bus technology itself but to a secondary effect of the conversion: freed from the fixed infrastructure that had anchored development, city governments and private developers redirected investment toward highways and suburban roads, which in turn made private automobile ownership more convenient and drew riders away from public transit altogether. In other words, the financial logic that favored buses over streetcars in isolation ultimately helped accelerate a broader shift away from public transit as a whole.

problem.question: According to the text, why did ridership decline on former streetcar corridors after they were converted to bus routes?
options: Because buses were cheaper to operate per mile, transit agencies cut back on route frequency and maintenance investment, and it was this direct cost-cutting that drove riders away from the former streetcar corridors.
Riders abandoned buses directly because bus technology itself was mechanically unreliable compared to streetcars on the same corridors.
The removal of fixed infrastructure indirectly encouraged investment in highways and suburban roads, which made driving more convenient and drew riders away from transit.
The decline in fare revenue caused by the conversion led city governments to redirect their own transit budgets into highway construction, which was the direct cause of falling ridership.
problem.explanation: 지문은 버스가 마일당 운영비는 더 저렴했음에도 불구하고 승차율이 감소했다는 역설을 제시하고, 그 진짜 원인을 '고정 인프라가 사라지면서 고속도로와 교외 도로에 투자가 몰렸고, 이것이 자동차 이용을 더 편리하게 만들어 대중교통 이용자를 빼앗아갔다'는 간접적·다단계 인과관계로 설명한다. C는 이 전체 인과 사슬을 정확히 반영한다. A는 지문과 반대로 버스가 더 비쌌다고 서술해 인과 방향을 뒤바꿨고, B는 지문이 '버스 기술 자체의 결함이 아니다'라고 명시적으로 부정한 원인을 제시했으며, D는 지문에 없는 '재정 관리 부실'이라는 근거 없는 내용을 지어냈다.
problem.explanationEn: The text presents a paradox: although buses were cheaper to operate per mile, ridership still declined, and it attributes this to an indirect, multi-step causal chain—removing fixed infrastructure led to investment shifting toward highways and suburban roads, which made cars more convenient and pulled riders away from transit. Choice C accurately captures this entire chain. Choice A reverses the cost relationship, claiming buses were more expensive when the text says the opposite. Choice B attributes the decline to mechanical unreliability, a cause the text explicitly rules out. Choice D invents an unsupported claim about financial mismanagement that never appears in the text.

problem.passage: For decades, marine biologists assumed that deep-sea coral reefs, which grow in total darkness thousands of meters below the surface, were largely isolated ecosystems sustained only by the slow rain of organic particles sinking from sunlit waters above. Recent surveys using submersible robots, however, have revealed that many deep-sea coral colonies thrive near underwater canyons where strong currents funnel nutrient-rich sediment from continental shelves directly to the reefs. These currents deliver far more organic material, and far more consistently, than the gradual particle rain ever could, allowing coral colonies near canyons to grow denser and support a greater diversity of fish than those in canyon-free regions. At the same time, researchers note that reefs far from any canyon still persist, albeit more sparsely, on particle rain alone, indicating that the canyon currents are not a strict requirement for survival but rather a supplemental resource that some reefs happen to exploit far more effectively than others.

problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Deep-sea coral reefs located near underwater canyons receive so much nutrient-rich sediment that reefs lacking access to canyon currents cannot survive at all.

Submersible robots have shown that underwater canyons are the primary cause of the biodiversity found in all deep-sea ecosystems, not just coral reefs.
Marine biologists have discovered that deep-sea coral reefs depend entirely on nutrient-rich sediment currents rather than on organic particles falling from the surface.
problem.explanation: 지문은 협곡 없는 산호초도 입자비만으로 생존한다는 점(조건)과, 협곡 근처 산호초는 추가로 풍부한 퇴적물 덕분에 더 밀도 높고 다양한 어류를 지원한다는 비교를 함께 제시한다. B는 이 두 요소—생존의 조건(입자비로도 가능)과 협곡의 보조적 이점(추가 자원으로 더 밀도 높은 성장)—를 모두 담고 있어 정답이다. A는 협곡 없는 곳은 생존조차 못한다고 범위를 과장했고(지문은 '더 드물게(sparsely)' 생존한다고 함), C는 산호초를 넘어 '모든 심해 생태계'로 초점을 잘못 확장했으며, D는 협곡 해류가 '유일한' 의존 대상인 것처럼 인과관계를 왜곡했다(지문은 보조 자원이라고 명시).
problem.explanationEn: The passage presents both a condition (reefs without canyons still survive on particle rain alone) and a comparison (canyon-adjacent reefs grow denser and more diverse due to an additional nutrient source). Choice B captures both elements—the survival condition and the supplemental benefit—making it correct. Choice A wrongly claims canyon-free reefs cannot survive at all, overstating the scope (the text says they persist 'more sparsely'). Choice C shifts focus beyond coral reefs to 'all deep-sea ecosystems,' which the text never claims. Choice D distorts the causal relationship by suggesting reefs depend 'entirely' on sediment currents, when the text explicitly calls them a supplemental, not required, resource.

problem.passage:
Botanists long believed that epiphytic orchids growing in the upper canopy of tropical cloud forests—rooted not in soil but on the bark of towering trees hundreds of meters above the forest floor—depended solely on mist and rainfall trapped by their spongy aerial roots for moisture and nutrients. Recent canopy-crane studies, however, have shown that many orchid colonies flourish near fog corridors, narrow gaps between ridgelines where warm valley air condenses into dense, mineral-laden fog that drifts continuously across exposed branches. This fog deposits calcium and nitrogen compounds far more steadily and in far greater quantity than ordinary rainfall, enabling orchids along these corridors to produce larger pseudobulbs and support a wider array of pollinating moths than orchids growing on trees away from any corridor. Nevertheless, botanists have also confirmed that orchids far from fog corridors continue to survive, though with noticeably slower growth and thinner root mats, relying on intermittent rain and dew alone; this suggests that fog-corridor exposure is not a precondition for an orchid's survival but rather an opportunistic bonus that certain colonies are positioned to exploit far more fully than their neighbors—only when ridgeline geometry channels the fog directly onto their branches, a condition unrelated to soil quality or tree species, does this advantage actually materialize.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Recent canopy-crane studies, however, have shown that many orchid colonies flourish near fog corridors, narrow gaps between ridgelines where warm valley air condenses into dense, mineral-laden fog that drifts continuously across exposed branches. This fog deposits calcium and nitrogen compounds far more steadily and in far greater quantity than ordinary rainfall, enabling orchids along these corridors to produce larger pseudobulbs and support a wider array of pollinating moths than orchids growing on trees away from any corridor. Nevertheless, botanists have also confirmed that orchids far from fog corridors continue to survive, though with noticeably slower growth and thinner root mats, relying on intermittent rain and dew alone; this suggests that fog-corridor exposure is not a precondition for an orchid's survival but rather an opportunistic bonus that certain colonies are positioned to exploit far more fully than their neighbors—only when ridgeline geometry channels the fog directly onto their branches, a condition unrelated to soil quality or tree species, does this advantage actually materialize.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Canopy-crane studies have proven that fog corridors are the single greatest driver of biodiversity across all cloud-forest canopy species, extending well beyond orchids alone.

Epiphytic orchids can persist on rain and dew alone, but those positioned within fog corridors gain access to a steadier, richer supply of minerals that fosters larger growth and greater pollinator diversity.
Because fog corridors supply calcium and nitrogen so reliably, orchids situated outside these corridors are generally unable to survive on the forest floor.
Botanists have determined that epiphytic orchids depend entirely on fog-corridor deposits rather than on rainfall, since rain alone cannot sustain pseudobulb growth.
problem.explanation: 지문은 두 가지를 종합해야 한다: (1) 협곡(=fog corridor)이 없어도 난초는 비와 이슬만으로 생존 가능하다는 조건, (2) 안개 통로에 위치한 난초는 추가로 풍부한 미네랄 덕분에 더 크게 자라고 더 다양한 수분매개 나방을 지원한다는 비교. 또한 'only when ridgeline geometry channels the fog directly'라는 조건절은 이 이점이 특정 지형 조건에서만 실현됨을 보여준다. B는 이 두 요소(생존의 최소조건+안개통로의 보조적 이점)를 모두 정확히 포착하여 정답이다. A는 초점을 '모든 캐노피 종'으로 범위 과장했다(지문은 난초에 국한). C는 안개 통로가 없으면 생존 자체가 불가능하다고 왜곡했는데, 지문은 '더 느리게, 더 얇은 뿌리로'라도 생존한다고 명시했으며 '숲 바닥'이라는 표현도 지문에 없는 오류다(착생란은 나무 위에서 자람). D는 안개 통로 의존을 '전적인' 것으로 인과관계를 전도시켰다—지문은 이를 보조적·기회적 자원이라고 명시했다.

quality.hardDesign: 결론(전략이 대수층 깊이에 따라 달라진다)이 한 문장에 직접 제시되지 않고, 대수층 근접/원거리 두 조건에 대한 서술과 'Only when researchers compared...'라는 조건절을 종합해야 도출되도록 설계했다. 오답 B는 정도 과장(완전 대체), C는 세부 기제를 중심 생각으로 오인, D는 인과관계 날조로, 모두 지문의 일부 어휘(fungal endophytes, stored rainwater, aquifer)를 공유해 근거 문장을 정확히 대조하지 않으면 걸러지지 않는다.

problem.passage:
Botanists once held that desert-dwelling barrel cacti in the Sonoran basin survived solely by storing rainwater in their thick stems, since the region's scorching daytime temperatures were thought to preclude any other means of moisture retention. Recent isotope-tracing studies, however, reveal that many barrel cacti harbor fungal endophytes within their root tissues, symbiotic fungi that draw moisture from deep subsurface aquifers and transfer it to the cactus in exchange for sugars. These fungal partners appear to supply a considerable portion of the cactus's water budget in areas overlying shallow aquifers, even though stored rainwater remains the dominant water source in outlying regions where aquifers lie too deep for fungal roots to reach. Only when researchers compared cacti across both zones did it become clear that a colony's water-acquisition strategy is not fixed but shifts according to the depth of the aquifer beneath it. As a result, botanists now contend that no single explanation can account for how barrel cacti endure the desert's extremes; rather, the mechanism depends on subsurface hydrological conditions that vary from one location to another.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Botanists once held that desert-dwelling barrel cacti in the Sonoran basin survived solely by storing rainwater in their thick stems, since the region's scorching daytime temperatures were thought to preclude any other means of moisture retention. Recent isotope-tracing studies, however, reveal that many barrel cacti harbor fungal endophytes within their root tissues, symbiotic fungi that draw moisture from deep subsurface aquifers and transfer it to the cactus in exchange for sugars. These fungal partners appear to supply a considerable portion of the cactus's water budget in areas overlying shallow aquifers, even though stored rainwater remains the dominant water source in outlying regions where aquifers lie too deep for fungal roots to reach. Only when researchers compared cacti across both zones did it become clear that a colony's water-acquisition strategy is not fixed but shifts according to the depth of the aquifer beneath it. As a result, botanists now contend that no single explanation can account for how barrel cacti endure the desert's extremes; rather, the mechanism depends on subsurface hydrological conditions that vary from one location to another.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Botanists have found that barrel cacti rely on different water-acquisition strategies depending on the depth of the aquifer located beneath a given colony.
Barrel cacti growing above shallow aquifers have stopped storing rainwater altogether, relying instead entirely on fungal endophytes for hydration.
Fungal endophytes transfer water to cacti in exchange for sugars, a symbiotic exchange that scientists previously believed was impossible in arid climates.
Stored rainwater is an unreliable water source in the Sonoran basin, which is why fungal endophytes have evolved to colonize cactus root systems there.
problem.explanation: 지문은 얕은 대수층 위에 있는 선인장은 균근내생균으로부터 상당한 수분을 얻고, 대수층이 깊은 지역에서는 여전히 저장된 빗물이 주된 수분원이라는 두 조건을 대비시킨 뒤, 'Only when researchers compared cacti across both zones'라는 조건절을 통해 전략이 위치(대수층 깊이)에 따라 달라진다는 종합적 결론을 이끌어낸다. A는 이 대수층 깊이에 따른 전략 차이라는 결론을 정확히 반영한다. B는 '완전히 그만두었다'는 강도 과장으로, 지문이 말한 '상당한 부분(considerable portion)'이라는 정도를 벗어나며 저장된 빗물이 다른 지역에서는 여전히 지배적이라는 대비를 무시한다. C는 화학적·생물학적 상호작용의 세부 기제에 초점을 맞추지만 이는 중심 생각이 아니라 뒷받침 정보일 뿐이며, '건조 기후에서는 불가능하다고 여겨졌다'는 내용은 지문에 없는 創作이다. D는 저장된 빗물이 불안정해서 균근내생균이 진화했다는 인과관계를 지어낸 것으로, 지문은 이러한 진화적 인과를 언급하지 않고 단지 위치에 따른 현재의 전략 차이만을 서술한다.

problem.passage: Art historians long treated the Dutch still-life paintings of the seventeenth century primarily as demonstrations of technical virtuosity, prized for their meticulous rendering of light on glass, fruit, and fabric. This view began to shift when scholars started paying closer attention to the specific objects depicted rather than merely the skill with which they were rendered. Wilted flowers positioned beside freshly bloomed ones, half-peeled lemons whose curling rinds seem to defy the otherwise still composition, and hourglasses tucked into the corners of otherwise opulent tables all recur with a frequency too consistent to be coincidental. Taken together, these recurring details suggest that many of these paintings were structured around a shared symbolic vocabulary warning viewers of the fleeting nature of material wealth and physical beauty, even as the paintings' surfaces celebrated exactly those things in lavish detail. Scholars now generally agree that appreciating the genre fully requires reading it on both levels: as a display of painterly skill and as a moral commentary embedded within that very display.
problem.stimulus: Art historians long treated the Dutch still-life paintings of the seventeenth century primarily as demonstrations of technical virtuosity, prized for their meticulous rendering of light on glass, fruit, and fabric. This view began to shift when scholars started paying closer attention to the specific objects depicted rather than merely the skill with which they were rendered. Wilted flowers positioned beside freshly bloomed ones, half-peeled lemons whose curling rinds seem to defy the otherwise still composition, and hourglasses tucked into the corners of otherwise opulent tables all recur with a frequency too consistent to be coincidental. Taken together, these recurring details suggest that many of these paintings were structured around a shared symbolic vocabulary warning viewers of the fleeting nature of material wealth and physical beauty, even as the paintings' surfaces celebrated exactly those things in lavish detail. Scholars now generally agree that appreciating the genre fully requires reading it on both levels: as a display of painterly skill and as a moral commentary embedded within that very display.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Dutch still-life paintings were created primarily to instruct viewers on the moral dangers of pursuing wealth rather than to showcase artistic skill.
The recurring presence of wilted flowers and hourglasses in Dutch still-life paintings proves that all seventeenth-century Dutch painters shared identical religious beliefs.
Full appreciation of Dutch still-life paintings requires recognizing that they function simultaneously as displays of technical skill and as symbolic commentary on the transience of material life.
Art historians initially misunderstood Dutch still-life paintings because they lacked the technical knowledge needed to interpret the paintings' brushwork and use of light.
problem.explanation: 지문은 네덜란드 정물화가 처음에는 기술적 정교함만으로 평가되었으나, 시든 꽃과 갓 핀 꽃의 대비, 반쯤 벗겨진 레몬, 모래시계 같은 반복 소재를 통해 물질적 부와 아름다움의 덧없음을 경고하는 상징적 어휘도 담고 있다는 점이 밝혀졌다고 설명하며, 이 두 층위를 함께 읽어야 한다는 학자들의 합의로 결론짓는다. C는 이 병존 관계를 정확히 반영한다. A는 상징적 논평만을 회화의 '주된' 목적으로 과장하여 지문이 강조한 '두 층위 모두'라는 균형을 깨뜨린다. B는 반복 소재로부터 '모든 화가가 동일한 종교적 신념을 공유했다'는 지나치게 넓은 결론을 지어내는데, 이는 지문에 근거가 없다. D는 미술사가들이 '기술적 지식이 부족해서' 오해했다는 원인을 지어낸 것으로, 지문은 단지 관심의 초점이 옮겨갔다고만 말했을 뿐 지식 부족을 언급하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage explains that Dutch still-life paintings were initially valued only for technical virtuosity, but recurring details—wilted versus fresh flowers, half-peeled lemons, hourglasses—reveal a symbolic vocabulary warning of the transience of wealth and beauty. The text concludes that scholars now agree the genre must be read on both levels simultaneously. Choice C accurately reflects this coexistence. Choice A overgeneralizes by claiming moral instruction was the 'primary' purpose, upsetting the balance the passage emphasizes. Choice B draws an unsupported and overly broad conclusion that all painters shared identical religious beliefs, which the text never claims. Choice D fabricates a cause (art historians lacking technical knowledge) for the initial misunderstanding, when the passage only says the scholarly focus shifted, not that earlier historians lacked expertise.

key_relations: 기존 관점(기술적 정교함)과 새로운 관점(상징적 경고)의 관계는 대체가 아니라 병존
반복되는 소재(시든 꽃, 모래시계 등)와 그것이 가리키는 상징적 의미의 연결
학자들의 현재 합의는 '두 수준 모두'를 함께 읽어야 한다는 것
design.answer_uses_relations: 정답은 기술적 정교함이라는 기존 관점과 상징적 경고라는 새로운 관점이 서로를 대체하는 것이 아니라 동시에 작동한다는 지문의 최종 결론을 정확히 종합한다.

distractor_design.relation: 상징적 경고라는 새 관점
반복되는 소재와 상징적 의미의 연결
기존 관점과 새 관점의 시간적 순서

design.target_difficulty_note: 정답을 찾으려면 두 관점(기술적 vs 상징적)이 대체 관계가 아니라 병존 관계라는 점을 정확히 종합해야 하며, 오답들은 한 관점만 과장하거나, 반복 소재에서 지나친 결론(모든 화가가 동일한 종교적 신념 공유)을 끌어내거나, 학자들이 기술적 지식이 부족해서 오해했다는 근거 없는 시간적 인과를 지어낸다.

problem.evidenceTarget: 지문 전체의 결론 — 네덜란드 정물화가 기술적 전시와 상징적 도덕적 논평이라는 두 층위로 동시에 읽혀야 한다는 중심 생각
problem.evidenceSpan: appreciating the genre fully requires reading it on both levels: as a display of painterly skill and as a moral commentary embedded within that very display
problem.answerRationale: 정답은 지문이 강조하는 두 층위(기술적 정교함과 상징적 경고)가 서로 배타적이지 않고 동시에 작동한다는 종합적 결론을 반영한다.

difficultyReasons: 정답을 고르기 위해 지문의 마지막 문장(두 수준 모두 읽어야 한다)을 정확히 종합해야 함(2단계 추론)
A와 C가 핵심 정보(상징적 경고, 기술적 정교함)를 공유하여 '대체 vs 병존' 관계를 정확히 구분해야 하므로 다소 미묘함
B는 과도한 일반화로 비교적 쉽게 배제 가능하여 난이도를 낮추는 요소
D는 인과관계 왜곡이 미묘하여 꼼꼼히 읽어야 배제 가능

distractors.plausibleBecause: 지문 후반부가 상징적 경고(모럴 커멘터리)에 강조점을 두는 것처럼 읽힐 수 있어 이 요소만 과도하게 취해 '주로'라는 표현으로 확대하면 그럴듯해 보인다
distractors.matches: 파괴적 아름다움과 부의 덧없음을 경고한다는 지문의 상징적 해석 부분과 일치
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 상징적 경고가 '기술적 기교를 대체'한다고 하지 않고, 두 가지가 동시에 작동한다고 결론짓는다. 'primarily...rather than'은 지문의 병존 관계를 단일 목적으로 왜곡한다

distractors.plausibleBecause: 반복되는 상징(시든 꽃, 모래시계)이 소재로 언급되어 이것이 정답의 핵심처럼 보일 수 있다
distractors.matches: 지문에서 언급된 구체적 소재(시든 꽃, 모래시계, 반쯤 벗긴 레몬)와 일치
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 이러한 소재가 '공유된 상징적 어휘'를 시사한다고만 말하지, 모든 화가가 동일한 종교적 신념을 가졌다는 과도한 결론을 내리지 않는다. 이는 지문에 없는 극단적 일반화이며 논리적 비약

distractors.plausibleBecause: 지문 초반에 '기존 관점이 오랫동안 지배적이었다'는 내용이 있어 미술사가들이 '오해'했다는 해석으로 이어질 수 있다
distractors.matches: 지문 첫 문장의 '미술사가들이 오랫동안 기술적 정교함으로만 다루었다'는 서술과 일치
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 미술사가들이 '기술 지식 부족'으로 오해했다고 말하지 않으며, 단지 관점이 구체적 소재에 주목하면서 '확장'되었다고 서술한다. 원인을 지식 부족으로 규정하는 것은 지문에 없는 추가된 인과관계

problem.passage: For decades, marine biologists assumed that deep-sea coral colonies, which grow in perpetual darkness thousands of meters below the surface, relied entirely on drifting organic matter, or "marine snow," for sustenance, since no sunlight reaches those depths to support photosynthetic algae. Recent submersible surveys, however, have found that many deep-sea corals host chemosynthetic bacteria within their tissues, microbes that convert dissolved hydrogen sulfide seeping from nearby cracks in the seafloor into usable energy. These bacterial partners appear to supply a substantial share of the coral's nutritional needs in areas near hydrothermal vents, even though marine snow remains the primary food source in vent-free regions farther from such seafloor fissures. Consequently, researchers now argue that the survival strategy of deep-sea corals cannot be reduced to a single mechanism but instead varies according to a colony's proximity to geochemical activity on the ocean floor.
problem.stimulus: For decades, marine biologists assumed that deep-sea coral colonies, which grow in perpetual darkness thousands of meters below the surface, relied entirely on drifting organic matter, or "marine snow," for sustenance, since no sunlight reaches those depths to support photosynthetic algae. Recent submersible surveys, however, have found that many deep-sea corals host chemosynthetic bacteria within their tissues, microbes that convert dissolved hydrogen sulfide seeping from nearby cracks in the seafloor into usable energy. These bacterial partners appear to supply a substantial share of the coral's nutritional needs in areas near hydrothermal vents, even though marine snow remains the primary food source in vent-free regions farther from such seafloor fissures. Consequently, researchers now argue that the survival strategy of deep-sea corals cannot be reduced to a single mechanism but instead varies according to a colony's proximity to geochemical activity on the ocean floor.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Deep-sea corals near hydrothermal vents have completely abandoned marine snow as a food source in favor of chemosynthetic bacteria.
Marine biologists have discovered that deep-sea corals obtain nourishment through different means depending on their location relative to seafloor geochemical activity.
Chemosynthetic bacteria convert hydrogen sulfide into energy, a process that was previously believed to occur only in shallow-water ecosystems.
Marine snow is an unreliable food source for deep-sea corals, which explains why so many coral colonies are found near hydrothermal vents.
problem.explanation: 지문은 심해 산호가 열수구 근처에서는 화학합성 박테리아로부터 상당한 영양을 얻고, 열수구가 없는 지역에서는 여전히 해양 눈에 주로 의존한다는 두 조건을 대비시킨 뒤, 이를 바탕으로 산호의 생존 전략이 단일하지 않고 위치에 따라 달라진다고 결론짓는다. B는 이 위치별 차이라는 종합적 결론을 정확히 반영한다. A는 '완전히 대체했다'는 강도 과장으로 지문이 말한 '상당한 몫'이라는 정도를 벗어난다. C는 화학합성 작용의 원리라는 세부에 초점을 맞추지만 이는 중심 생각이 아니라 뒷받침 정보일 뿐이며, '얕은 물에서만 일어난다고 믿어졌다'는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 해양 눈이 불안정해서 산호가 열수구 근처에 분포한다는 인과관계를 지어낸 것으로 지문에 근거가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage contrasts two conditions: near hydrothermal vents, chemosynthetic bacteria supply a substantial share of coral nutrition, while in vent-free areas marine snow remains the primary food source. The passage concludes that coral survival strategy is not reducible to one mechanism but varies by location. Choice B accurately captures this location-based synthesis. Choice A overstates the intensity, claiming corals have 'completely abandoned' marine snow, which contradicts the passage's qualified language ('substantial share'). Choice C focuses on a supporting mechanistic detail (how bacteria convert sulfide) rather than the main idea, and its claim about shallow-water ecosystems is unsupported. Choice D invents a causal relationship (marine snow's unreliability explaining coral distribution near vents) that the text never states.

key_relations: 열수구 인접 지역 vs 비인접 지역이라는 위치 조건에 따른 먹이원 차이
화학합성 박테리아는 '상당 부분'을 공급하지, 전적으로 대체하지는 않음
기존 통념(해양 눈에만 의존)과 새로운 발견(화학합성 공생)의 관계

design.target_difficulty_note: 정답을 찾으려면 두 조건(위치)과 두 먹이원의 상대적 비중을 모두 종합해야 하며, 오답들은 강도 과장, 세부 초점 이동, 인과관계 왜곡이라는 서로 다른 방식으로 틀렸다.

problem.evidenceTarget: 지문 전체의 결론 — 심해 산호의 영양 공급 전략이 단일하지 않고 위치 조건에 따라 달라진다는 중심 생각
problem.evidenceSpan: researchers now argue that the survival strategy of deep-sea corals cannot be reduced to a single mechanism but instead varies according to a colony's proximity to geochemical activity on the ocean floor
problem.answerRationale: 정답은 지문이 제시한 두 가지 조건(열수구 인접/비인접)에 따라 영양 공급 방식이 달라진다는 종합 결론을 정확히 반영한다.

difficultyReasons: 정답을 고르려면 지문 전체 논지(위치에 따른 다른 전략)를 종합해야 하며 단일 문장 인용으로는 부족함
오답 A는 정답과 핵심 소재(화학합성 박테리아 기여)를 공유하면서 강도만 다르게 왜곡해 변별에 주의가 필요함
오답 C는 지문에 없는 정보(얕은 바다 통념)를 추가한 것으로 비교적 명백히 배제 가능함
오답 D는 인과관계를 임의로 만들어낸 것으로 지문을 재확인하면 배제되지만 표면적으로는 그럴듯함

distractors.plausibleBecause: 지문에 열수구 근처에서 화학합성 박테리아가 상당 부분의 영양을 공급한다는 내용이 있어, 이를 과장하면 그럴듯해 보임
distractors.matches: 'These bacterial partners appear to supply a substantial share of the coral's nutritional needs in areas near hydrothermal vents' 부분과 일부 일치
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 '상당 부분(substantial share)'이라고만 했지 '완전히 대체(completely abandoned)'했다고 하지 않음 — 강도를 과장한 오류

distractors.plausibleBecause: 화학합성 박테리아가 황화수소를 에너지로 전환한다는 지문 내용과 일치하여 그럴듯해 보임
distractors.matches: 'microbes that convert dissolved hydrogen sulfide seeping from nearby cracks in the seafloor into usable energy' 부분과 일치
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 이 과정이 얕은 바다에서만 일어난다고 믿어졌다는 언급이 전혀 없음 — 지문에 없는 정보를 추가한 오류이며 세부사항이지 중심 생각도 아님

distractors.plausibleBecause: 해양 눈이 비신뢰적이라는 인상과 산호가 열수구 근처에 분포한다는 내용을 결합해 인과관계처럼 보이게 함
distractors.matches: 'marine snow remains the primary food source in vent-free regions' 및 열수구 근처 산호 언급과 표면적으로 연결됨
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 해양 눈이 '불신뢰적'이라거나 그것이 산호가 열수구 근처에 많이 분포하는 '이유'라고 말하지 않음 — 근거 없는 인과관계를 지어낸 오류

problem.passage:
Art historians long treated the sudden proliferation of vividly colored pigments in fifteenth-century Flemish panel paintings as evidence of growing artistic ambition, arguing that painters were consciously pushing toward greater chromatic boldness as a mark of skill. Technical analysis of paint samples, however, has complicated this narrative. Chemical dating shows that the expansion of the color palette closely tracks the opening of new overland trade routes through Central Asia, which made previously rare mineral pigments, such as lapis lazuli, dramatically cheaper and more available to workshops outside the wealthiest courts. Where trade routes were disrupted by regional conflicts, panel paintings from the same period and region show a marked reduction in the use of these expensive pigments, even among painters whose documented ambitions and reputations remained unchanged. This correlation suggests that the visual transformation of Flemish painting during this era was driven less by a shift in artistic intention than by fluctuations in the economic accessibility of materials, with painters' stylistic choices constrained or enabled by what pigments the market could supply at a given time.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Art historians long treated the sudden proliferation of vividly colored pigments in fifteenth-century Flemish panel paintings as evidence of growing artistic ambition, arguing that painters were consciously pushing toward greater chromatic boldness as a mark of skill. Technical analysis of paint samples, however, has complicated this narrative. Chemical dating shows that the expansion of the color palette closely tracks the opening of new overland trade routes through Central Asia, which made previously rare mineral pigments, such as lapis lazuli, dramatically cheaper and more available to workshops outside the wealthiest courts. Where trade routes were disrupted by regional conflicts, panel paintings from the same period and region show a marked reduction in the use of these expensive pigments, even among painters whose documented ambitions and reputations remained unchanged. This correlation suggests that the visual transformation of Flemish painting during this era was driven less by a shift in artistic intention than by fluctuations in the economic accessibility of materials, with painters' stylistic choices constrained or enabled by what pigments the market could supply at a given time.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Fifteenth-century Flemish painters intentionally reduced their use of expensive pigments whenever regional conflicts disrupted trade routes through Central Asia.
The increased use of vivid pigments in Flemish paintings was driven mainly by trade-based shifts in material availability rather than by changes in artistic ambition.

Lapis lazuli and other rare pigments became so central to the story that the text treats their pricing as the single most important detail, more important than the overall shift away from artistic-intention explanations.

Chemical dating of paint samples reveals that pigment availability, not conflict-driven trade disruptions, was the sole factor art historians historically credited for the chromatic shifts in Flemish panel paintings.
problem.explanation:
지문은 (1) 미술사학자들의 기존 통설(예술적 야망이 색채 확장의 원인)을 소개한 뒤, (2) 화학적 연대 분석 결과 안료 사용량이 무역로 개통/단절과 상관관계를 보이며, 화가의 명성과 야망이 그대로였음에도 무역 단절 시 안료 사용이 줄었다는 증거를 제시하고, (3) 마지막 문장에서 이를 종합해 '예술적 의도보다 재료의 경제적 접근성'이 색채 변화의 주된 동인이라고 결론짓는다. 이 논증 구조의 최종 결론을 그대로 담은 B가 중심 생각이다.

A는 무역 단절과 안료 감소의 상관관계(단계2)는 반영하지만, 이를 화가의 '의도적' 선택으로 왜곡한다 — 지문은 오히려 화가의 야망이 불변이었음을 근거로 '의도가 아니'라고 강조하므로, 지문에 없는 인과를 지어낸 것이다(UNSUPPORTED_BY_TEXT).

C는 라피스 라줄리가 저렴해졌다는 세부(단계2의 일부)는 맞지만, '모든 다른 안료를 포기했다'는 것은 지문에 없는 과도한 일반화다(OVERGENERALIZED).

D는 미술사학자들의 통설(단계1)을 언급하지만, 그 통설이 원래 '예술적 야망' 쪽이었다는 사실과 반대로 처음부터 경제적 설명에 합의했다고 서술해, 지문의 논증 흐름(통설→반증→결론) 대신 엉뚱한 지점에 초점을 맞춘다(WRONG_FOCUS).
problem.evidenceTarget: 지문 전체의 중심 생각 — 플랑드르 회화의 색채 변화가 예술적 의도가 아니라 무역로에 따른 재료 접근성 변화로 설명된다는 결론
problem.evidenceSpan: This correlation suggests that the visual transformation of Flemish painting during this era was driven less by a shift in artistic intention than by fluctuations in the economic accessibility of materials
problem.answerRationale: 단계1(기존 통설 제시: 예술적 야망) → 단계2(반증 증거: 안료 사용량이 무역로 개통/단절과 상관관계를 보이고, 화가의 야망·명성은 불변이었음에도 무역 단절 시 안료 사용 감소) → 단계3(결론: 색채 변화의 주된 동인은 예술적 의도가 아니라 재료의 경제적 접근성). 선택지 B는 이 단계3의 결론과 정확히 일치하므로 정답이며, 나머지 선택지는 단계2 또는 단계1의 일부만 반영하거나 이를 왜곡한다.

difficultyReasons: 정답과 오답 A가 공유하는 정보(무역 붕괴-안료 감소)가 많아 인과관계의 방향(의도 vs 제약)을 정확히 구분해야 함
오답 D는 미술사학자들의 기존 견해와 실제 원인을 혼동시켜 정확한 독해가 필요함
오답 C는 명백히 지엽적 세부사항에 집중하여 비교적 쉽게 배제 가능

distractors.plausibleBecause: 지문에 무역로 붕괴와 안료 사용 감소의 상관관계가 언급되어, 화가들이 의도적으로 줄였다는 인과관계로 오독할 수 있음
distractors.matches: regional conflicts로 인한 안료 사용 감소 부분
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 화가들의 '의도'가 아니라 시장의 재료 공급 가능성이 원인이라고 명시하며, 오히려 화가들의 야망과 평판은 변하지 않았다고 강조함으로써 의도적 선택이 아님을 부정함

distractors.plausibleBecause: 라피스라줄리가 지문에서 구체적 예시로 반복 언급되어 중요해 보임
distractors.matches: lapis lazuli 언급 부분
distractors.whyWrong: 이는 세부 예시일 뿐이며 지문의 주제문(안료 가용성이 예술적 의도보다 더 큰 요인)과 무관하게 텍스트의 서술 방식 자체를 잘못 평가함; 지문이 가격을 '가장 중요한 세부사항'으로 취급한다는 주장은 근거 없음

distractors.plausibleBecause: 화학적 연대측정이 안료 가용성을 밝혀냈다는 부분과 미술사학자들의 기존 견해를 언급하여 그럴듯해 보임
distractors.matches: chemical dating과 art historians의 기존 주장 부분
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 안료 가용성이 '유일한' 요인이라거나 미술사학자들이 갈등에 의한 무역 붕괴를 원인으로 여겼다고 말하지 않음; 오히려 기존 미술사학자들은 예술적 야망을 원인으로 보았다고 명시함

problem.passage: For decades, marine biologists assumed that deep-sea coral reefs, which grow in total darkness thousands of meters below the surface, were simply slow-motion, low-diversity versions of their shallow-water counterparts. Recent submersible surveys of reefs off the Atlantic coast have complicated this picture. While deep-sea corals do grow far more slowly than shallow reef corals, some surveyed structures have been dated to over 40,000 years old, making them among the oldest continuously living ecosystems on Earth, and they host invertebrate communities whose species richness rivals that of many shallow reefs. However, researchers caution that this apparent resilience is deceptive: because deep-sea corals grow so slowly and depend on a narrow band of stable temperature and chemistry, damage from bottom trawling or deep-sea mining can take centuries to repair, if the reefs recover at all, whereas comparably damaged shallow reefs often show partial regrowth within a few decades.
problem.stimulus: For decades, marine biologists assumed that deep-sea coral reefs, which grow in total darkness thousands of meters below the surface, were simply slow-motion, low-diversity versions of their shallow-water counterparts. Recent submersible surveys of reefs off the Atlantic coast have complicated this picture. While deep-sea corals do grow far more slowly than shallow reef corals, some surveyed structures have been dated to over 40,000 years old, making them among the oldest continuously living ecosystems on Earth, and they host invertebrate communities whose species richness rivals that of many shallow reefs. However, researchers caution that this apparent resilience is deceptive: because deep-sea corals grow so slowly and depend on a narrow band of stable temperature and chemistry, damage from bottom trawling or deep-sea mining can take centuries to repair, if the reefs recover at all, whereas comparably damaged shallow reefs often show partial regrowth within a few decades.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Deep-sea coral reefs are far older than shallow reefs but contain fewer invertebrate species because of the darkness in which they grow.
Although deep-sea coral reefs turn out to be surprisingly old and diverse, their slow growth makes them especially vulnerable to lasting damage from human activity.
Submersible surveys have shown that bottom trawling and deep-sea mining are the primary causes of coral decline in both deep and shallow reef environments.
Deep-sea corals depend on a narrow range of temperature and chemical conditions, which explains why they grow more slowly than shallow-water corals.
problem.explanation: 지문은 두 부분으로 구성된다: (1) 심해 산호초가 기존 통념과 달리 매우 오래되었고 종 다양성도 얕은 산호초에 필적한다는 새로운 발견, (2) 하지만 느린 성장 속도 때문에 트롤 어업이나 심해 채굴로 인한 손상이 수백 년이 지나도 회복되지 않을 수 있다는 경고. B는 이 두 요소(뜻밖의 나이·다양성 + 취약성)를 모두 정확히 포괄하므로 정답이다. A는 다양성이 낮다고 잘못 말해 지문의 핵심 발견(다양성이 얕은 산호초에 필적한다)을 왜곡한다(범위 오류). C는 손상의 '원인'이 두 환경 모두에 동일하게 적용된다고 확대 해석하지만, 지문은 회복 속도의 '차이'를 강조하지, 원인이 같다는 주장을 하지 않는다(인과 왜곡). D는 느린 성장의 원인(좁은 온도·화학 조건)만 다루고, 그것이 왜 중요한지(회복 불가능성)라는 지문의 핵심 결론을 빠뜨린다(인과적 초점 이동, 세부사항에 그침).
problem.explanationEn: The passage has two parts: (1) a surprising finding that deep-sea coral reefs are far older than assumed and rival shallow reefs in species diversity, and (2) a warning that because of their slow growth, damage from trawling or mining may never fully heal. Choice B captures both the surprising age/diversity and the resulting vulnerability, making it the main idea. Choice A wrongly claims lower diversity, contradicting the passage's key finding that diversity rivals shallow reefs (a scope distortion). Choice C overextends the causal claim, suggesting the same causes equally damage both reef types, when the passage's point is about the difference in recovery time, not shared causation. Choice D only explains why deep-sea corals grow slowly but omits the passage's central conclusion about why that slow growth matters (irreversible damage), making it too narrow a detail.

key_relations: 나이·다양성에 대한 새로운 발견(오래됨+높은 다양성)과 기존 통념(단순하고 다양성 낮음)의 대조
느린 성장 속도라는 원인이 손상 시 회복 불가능이라는 결과로 이어짐(원인-결과)
심해 산호초와 얕은 산호초의 손상 회복 속도 비교(수십 년 vs 수백 년/영구)
design.answer_uses_relations: 정답은 '놀랍게도 오래되고 다양하다'는 발견과 '느린 성장 때문에 손상이 영구적일 수 있다'는 결론을 모두 포괄해, 지문 전체의 논지(회복력이 있어 보이지만 실은 취약하다)를 정확히 요약한다.

distractor_design.relation: 나이-다양성 대조
원인-결과(손상 원인)
느린 성장의 원인

problem.evidenceTarget: 지문 전체가 전달하는 중심 생각 — 심해 산호초의 뜻밖의 나이·다양성과 그로 인한 취약성
problem.evidenceSpan: researchers caution that this apparent resilience is deceptive: because deep-sea corals grow so slowly and depend on a narrow band of stable temperature and chemistry, damage from bottom trawling or deep-sea mining can take centuries to repair
problem.answerRationale: 지문은 심해 산호초가 오래되고 다양성이 높다는 놀라운 발견을 제시한 뒤, 느린 성장 때문에 손상 회복이 사실상 불가능하다는 경고로 마무리되므로, 두 요소를 모두 담은 선택지가 중심 생각이다.

difficultyReasons: 정답을 고르려면 지문 전체(발견+경고)의 두 요소를 모두 포괄하는 선택지를 찾아야 함(종합 추론)
오답들이 지문의 실제 세부 정보(나이, 다양성, 트롤링, 온도 의존)를 사용해 그럴듯하게 구성되어 있어 표면적 일치가 강함
A는 지문과 반대 방향의 비교(다양성이 낮다 vs rivals)를 담고 있어 정독하면 배제 가능하지만 빠르게 읽으면 매력적임
C와 D는 세부사항을 중심 생각으로 착각하게 만드는 scope/causal 오류로 설계되어 변별력이 있음

distractors.plausibleBecause: 지문이 오래됨과 다양성을 언급하므로 나이와 다양성에 관한 비교로 착각할 수 있음

problem.passage: Art historians have long debated why Dutch still-life painters of the seventeenth century so frequently included wilting flowers, overturned glasses, and half-peeled fruit alongside their most lavishly rendered banquet tables. One common interpretation treats these details purely as moralizing symbols, reminders of mortality inserted to counterbalance the paintings' evident celebration of material wealth. Yet a closer examination of contemporary Dutch trade records complicates this reading: many of the specific flowers depicted, such as tulips and irises out of season, could not have been physically present together at any single sitting, since they bloomed at different times of year and had to be painted from separate studies made months apart. This practical detail suggests that the paintings were never intended as literal records of an actual table at all, but rather as constructed composites designed to display the painter's technical range and, implicitly, the sitter's access to rare and expensive goods across an entire growing season. Read this way, the presence of decay within the image serves less as an isolated moral warning and more as one element within a broader demonstration of abundance, skill, and status that the moralizing interpretation, taken alone, does not fully explain.

Evidence that these paintings combine flowers from different seasons suggests they were composite displays of wealth and skill, a purpose the purely moralizing interpretation fails to fully capture.

problem.explanation: 지문은 서로 다른 계절에 피는 꽃들이 한 그림에 함께 등장한다는 사실이 그림이 실제 상차림의 기록이 아니라 부와 기술을 과시하기 위한 합성 구성물이라는 것을 시사하며, 부패의 이미지도 이러한 과시의 일부로 재해석되어야 한다고 주장한다. A는 계절이 다른 꽃을 따로 그린 이유를 '겨울철 접근성 부족'으로 잘못 설명하는데, 지문은 이를 인과가 아니라 합성물이라는 증거로 사용한다. B는 전통적인 도덕적 해석을 그대로 반복하지만, 지문은 이 해석이 유일한 목적이 아니라 불완전하다고 명시한다. D는 튤립과 아이리스가 '가장 비싼 꽃'이었다는 근거 없는 주장을 하며, 무역 기록이 실제로 증명하는 바(계절적 불일치)를 벗어난다. 따라서 정답은 C번이다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage argues that the fact different-season flowers appear together in one painting indicates the works are composite constructions displaying wealth and skill, not literal records, and that decay should be reinterpreted as part of this broader display rather than a purely moral message. Choice A wrongly explains the separate studies as due to winter accessibility, when the text uses this fact as evidence of composite construction, not a causal explanation. Choice B simply repeats the traditional moralizing interpretation, which the text says is incomplete, not the sole purpose. Choice D makes an unsupported claim that tulips and irises were the 'most expensive' flowers, going beyond what the trade records actually establish (seasonal mismatch). Therefore, the correct answer is C.

problem.passage:
For decades, marine biologists assumed that deep-sea hydrothermal vent communities were essentially isolated evolutionary islands, each vent field developing its own unique fauna in near-total genetic isolation from neighboring fields separated by hundreds of kilometers of inhospitable seafloor. This view was based on the observation that many vent species, such as certain tubeworms and vent crabs, have relatively short-lived larval stages that seemed insufficient for crossing such vast distances. However, recent genetic surveys comparing populations across the East Pacific Rise and the Galápagos Rift have revealed surprisingly low genetic divergence between geographically distant vent communities, suggesting that larvae are transported far greater distances than their short lifespans would predict. Researchers now propose that deep ocean currents, rather than larval swimming ability alone, act as long-distance dispersal corridors, carrying larvae in a dormant or semi-dormant state that extends their effective survival time. This revised understanding implies that vent ecosystems, though visually isolated on the seafloor, are functionally interconnected through subsurface currents, and that conservation efforts protecting a single vent field cannot be assumed to preserve a genetically distinct population.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: For decades, marine biologists assumed that deep-sea hydrothermal vent communities were essentially isolated evolutionary islands, each vent field developing its own unique fauna in near-total genetic isolation from neighboring fields separated by hundreds of kilometers of inhospitable seafloor. This view was based on the observation that many vent species, such as certain tubeworms and vent crabs, have relatively short-lived larval stages that seemed insufficient for crossing such vast distances. However, recent genetic surveys comparing populations across the East Pacific Rise and the Galápagos Rift have revealed surprisingly low genetic divergence between geographically distant vent communities, suggesting that larvae are transported far greater distances than their short lifespans would predict. Researchers now propose that deep ocean currents, rather than larval swimming ability alone, act as long-distance dispersal corridors, carrying larvae in a dormant or semi-dormant state that extends their effective survival time. This revised understanding implies that vent ecosystems, though visually isolated on the seafloor, are functionally interconnected through subsurface currents, and that conservation efforts protecting a single vent field cannot be assumed to preserve a genetically distinct population.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.explanation: 지문의 논리는 (1) 짧은 유생 수명 때문에 열수구 군집들이 고립되어 있다는 기존 통념 제시 → (2) 그러나 East Pacific Rise와 Galápagos Rift 사이 유전자 조사에서 예상보다 훨씬 낮은 유전적 차이가 발견됨 → (3) 이는 해류가 유생을 장거리로 운반하기 때문이라는 설명 → (4) 따라서 열수구 생태계는 겉보기와 달리 실제로는 해류를 통해 연결되어 있고, 하나의 열수구만 보호하는 보전 정책은 유전적으로 독립된 개체군을 보존한다고 볼 수 없다는 결론으로 이어진다. 이 인과적 흐름 전체(통념→반증하는 유전자 증거→해류라는 원인→연결성이라는 결론)를 포착한 선택지는 C뿐이다. A는 유생 수명에 대한 세부사항을 지문과 반대로(더 짧다고) 왜곡했고 지문에 그런 언급이 없다(UNSUPPORTED_BY_TEXT). B는 '동일한 종 구성'이라는, 지문이 말한 '낮은 유전적 차이'를 넘어서는 과장된 주장이다(OVERGENERALIZED). D는 보전 노력이 '실패했다'는, 지문의 실제 결론(전제를 재검토해야 한다)이 아닌 엉뚱한 초점으로 빗나갔다(WRONG_FOCUS).
problem.evidenceTarget: 지문 전체를 관통하는 중심 생각: 유전자 증거가 열수구 생태계의 '고립' 통념을 뒤집고, 이 생태계가 해류를 통해 실제로는 연결되어 있음을 보여준다는 것
problem.evidenceSpan: recent genetic surveys comparing populations across the East Pacific Rise and the Galápagos Rift have revealed surprisingly low genetic divergence between geographically distant vent communities, suggesting that larvae are transported far greater distances than their short lifespans would predict
problem.answerRationale: 1) 지문은 먼저 '짧은 유생 수명 → 고립'이라는 기존 통념을 제시한다. 2) 이어서 제시된 evidence_span(먼 거리 군집 간 낮은 유전적 차이)은 이 통념과 정면으로 모순되는 관찰이다. 3) 지문은 이 모순을 해류에 의한 장거리 유생 운반이라는 원인으로 설명하며, 4) 그 결과로 '시각적으로는 고립되어 보이지만 기능적으로는 연결되어 있다'는 새로운 결론을 도출한다. 따라서 중심 생각은 단순히 유전자 조사 결과 자체(세부사항)가 아니라, 그 결과가 기존의 '고립' 통념을 어떻게 뒤집는가라는 인과적 전환에 있다. 정답 C만이 '새로운 증거 → 통념에 대한 도전'이라는 이 전환 구조 전체를 포착한다.

problem.passage:
When city planners in the early twentieth century began separating urban land into distinct zones for housing, commerce, and industry, the practice of zoning was promoted primarily as a public health measure, intended to keep noxious factories away from residential neighborhoods. Over time, however, zoning ordinances expanded far beyond this original purpose, coming to dictate minimum lot sizes, parking requirements, and building heights even in areas with no industrial activity nearby. This expansion had an unintended consequence that planners rarely anticipated: by mandating low-density, single-use development across vast swaths of cities, zoning made it structurally difficult to build the kind of mixed, walkable neighborhoods that had been common before the practice existed. As a result, residents in many mid-century cities found themselves dependent on automobiles for even short trips, not because they preferred driving but because the zoning code itself had made walking or transit-based living increasingly impractical. Some historians now argue that this dependency, often attributed to postwar consumer preference for cars, was in substantial part a byproduct of regulatory choices made decades earlier for reasons entirely unrelated to transportation.

According to the text, what does the passage suggest about automobile dependency in mid-century cities?
problem.stimulus: When city planners in the early twentieth century began separating urban land into distinct zones for housing, commerce, and industry, the practice of zoning was promoted primarily as a public health measure, intended to keep noxious factories away from residential neighborhoods. Over time, however, zoning ordinances expanded far beyond this original purpose, coming to dictate minimum lot sizes, parking requirements, and building heights even in areas with no industrial activity nearby. This expansion had an unintended consequence that planners rarely anticipated: by mandating low-density, single-use development across vast swaths of cities, zoning made it structurally difficult to build the kind of mixed, walkable neighborhoods that had been common before the practice existed. As a result, residents in many mid-century cities found themselves dependent on automobiles for even short trips, not because they preferred driving but because the zoning code itself had made walking or transit-based living increasingly impractical. Some historians now argue that this dependency, often attributed to postwar consumer preference for cars, was in substantial part a byproduct of regulatory choices made decades earlier for reasons entirely unrelated to transportation.
problem.question: According to the text, what does the passage suggest about automobile dependency in mid-century cities?
options: It resulted mainly from zoning ordinances that were originally designed to separate noxious factories from residential neighborhoods for public health reasons.
It arose in substantial part from regulatory decisions about land use that were unrelated to transportation, rather than solely from residents' preference for cars.
It was a direct and intended outcome that planners deliberately built into zoning codes once they realized how popular automobiles had become.
It occurred because zoning ordinances mandated minimum lot sizes and parking requirements specifically in order to encourage residents to drive rather than walk.
problem.explanation: 지문은 자동차 의존이 흔히 소비자의 자동차 선호 때문이라고 여겨지지만, 실제로는 교통과 무관한 이유로 만들어진 조닝 규제의 부산물이라고 주장한다. A는 조닝의 '원래' 목적(공중보건)을 원인으로 제시하지만, 지문은 확장된 이후의 조닝(용지 규모, 주차 요건 등)이 원인이라고 명시하므로 시간 관계를 혼동한 오답이다. C는 계획가들이 의도적으로 자동차 의존을 유도했다고 주장하지만 지문은 이를 '예상치 못한 결과(unintended consequence)'라고 명시하여 인과관계를 정반대로 왜곡한다. D는 특정 조항(최소 부지 크기, 주차 요건)이 '운전을 장려하기 위해' 만들어졌다고 하지만, 지문은 이 조항들의 원래 의도가 운전 장려가 아니었음을 분명히 한다. 따라서 정답은 B번이다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage argues that automobile dependency, often blamed on consumer preference, was actually substantially a byproduct of zoning regulations enacted for reasons unrelated to transportation. Choice A cites zoning's original purpose (public health) as the cause, but the text specifies that it was the later expanded zoning (lot sizes, parking, etc.) that caused dependency—a temporal confusion. Choice C claims planners intentionally built in car dependency, but the text explicitly calls this an 'unintended consequence,' reversing the causal relationship. Choice D claims specific provisions were made 'in order to' encourage driving, but the text makes clear these provisions were not originally intended for that purpose. Therefore, the correct answer is B.

key_relations: zoning's original purpose (public health/factory separation) versus its later expanded scope (lot sizes, parking, height)
causal link between expanded zoning and structural difficulty of building walkable neighborhoods
the reinterpretation: car dependency attributed to consumer preference vs. actually a byproduct of unrelated regulatory choices
design.answer_uses_relations: The correct choice captures the reattribution the text makes: dependency is substantially a byproduct of regulatory decisions unrelated to transportation, not simply consumer preference, without overstating this as the sole or original cause.

distractor_design.relation: zoning's original public-health purpose
the causal link between zoning and car dependency
specific expanded provisions (lot sizes, parking requirements)
